About.title: About devKit
About.intro: devKit is a free toolkit for people who build, test, or study software. This page explains what the project does, who it is for, what it does not do, and how to reach the people who run the site.

s1.heading: What devKit is
s1.body:
devKit (devkit.example.com) is a set of generators, validators, and utilities for concrete development tasks: build a CPF with check digits, validate a numeric CNPJ, create a QR code, inspect a JWT, convert a file to Base64, or look up an HTTP status.

Each tool has its own page, with the control to generate or validate and copy that explains the format, the limit of the result, and, when the algorithm matters, how the math works. The CPF page, for example, describes the mask, modulo 11, and the difference between a mathematically valid number and a record at Brazil’s tax authority.

There is no required account and no paid plan for basic use. Open the tool, generate or check the value, and copy the result.

s2.heading: Who it is for
s2.body:
Developers use devKit for seeds, mocks, and sample payloads. A masked CPF exercises a front-end input; a UUID avoids collisions in tests; a sample JWT shows header and payload before you connect a real identity provider.

QA builds staging scenarios: a numeric CNPJ, a digitable line in boleto format, an IBAN with a valid checksum, a QR code pointing at a staging URL. The value exists so the application can react, not so it can impersonate a person.

Students and anyone learning to program get the calculation next to the result. You can see why a repeated-digit sequence is not a valid CPF, why Base64 is not encryption, and what each HTTP status range means.

s3.heading: What devKit is not
s3.body:
devKit is not a government service, does not look up CPF or CNPJ in an official database, and does not issue documents. Generated numbers are synthetic: they can pass a check-digit test and still not exist as a person or company record.

Do not use the output for fraud, account opening, invoices, contracts, sign-up at a bank or carrier, or to impersonate someone else. That use is forbidden by the [Terms of Use](/termos) and may be a crime. Test data stays in a test environment.

If you need a real document, stop. The right channel is the official agency, not a test generator.

s4.heading: How the tools work
s4.body:
Generation and validation run in your browser. The CPF, QR text, JWT, and file you convert to Base64 are not uploaded to devKit just because you used the tool. Favorites, some generator history, theme, and dynamic QR campaigns stay in your browser’s local storage.

What leaves the device is a normal page visit and, only if you write one, a [Contact](/contato) message. The [Privacy Policy](/privacidade) covers analytics, ads, and the form processor.

s5.heading: Editorial content
s5.body:
Besides the catalog, the [blog](/blog) publishes guides on the same topics: CPF check digits, when a dynamic QR code helps, what to look at in a JWT. Tool pages repeat the essentials for people who land from search, so the article is not the only explanation.

The homepage groups tools into documents, codes, international, security, productivity, and math. Search and favorites bring back what you already use.

The site is operated by the devKit team. The public channel is [contact@example.com](mailto:contact@example.com) and the [Contact](/contato) form. We do not publish a phone number.

Use that channel for bugs, suggestions, and privacy requests. Do not send passwords, production tokens, a real customer document, or someone else’s personal data. Name the page, what you expected, and what happened.

s1.heading: Who is responsible
s1.body:
The team that operates devKit is responsible for information you send through the contact form and for the cookie and script choices on this site. To request access, correction, or deletion, write to [contact@example.com](mailto:contact@example.com) or use the [Contact](/contato) page.

There is no published support phone number. We do not ask for an identity document to use the tools.

s2.heading: What we collect
s2.body:
Contact form. Name, email, and message are sent through Web3Forms to contact@example.com, only so we can reply. Do not put a password, token, or real customer data in that form.

In-browser tools. Generating or validating CPF, CNPJ, QR codes, Base64, JWT, and similar utilities happens on your device. That content is not sent to devKit merely because you used the tool. Favorites, local history, theme, and dynamic QR campaigns stay in browser storage (localStorage) and you can delete them by clearing site data.

Measurement and ads. The site loads Google Analytics (aggregate audience), Microsoft Clarity (heatmaps and session replay), and Google AdSense for ads. Those providers may receive technical identifiers, pages viewed, and, with Clarity, a replay of how you interact with the page. We do not intentionally submit tool output to those services, but a third-party script can record what is visible on screen.

Hosting logs. Vercel and the delivery network may log IP, user-agent, and URL for security and operations.

Sign-in. If an account UI is shown, Clerk processes the account email and session under its own policy. The tools do not require an account.

s3.heading: Why we use it
s3.body:
To reply to support, correction, and privacy messages. To operate the site and understand, in aggregate, which pages are used. To show ads so the tools can stay free. To meet a legal duty when a valid authority request exists.

We do not sell contact lists. We do not use the form for an automatic newsletter.

s4.heading: Cookies and similar technologies
s4.body:
Essential cookies and local storage remember preferences such as theme. Analytics and advertising cookies and identifiers come from Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity, and Google AdSense when those scripts load.

You can block third-party cookies and scripts in the browser or with a privacy extension. That can stop personalized ads and audience measurement. Tools that run only in the browser remain usable.

Clarity may mask some of what you type, but do not assume every keystroke is hidden: do not paste production secrets on any page.

s5.heading: Google AdSense

We may use Google AdSense to show ads. Google and its partners may use cookies to serve ads based on visits to this site or others.

You can turn off personalized ads in [Google Ads Settings](https://www.google.com/settings/ads). Google’s policy describes what the provider does with those identifiers. An ad does not change a tool’s result.

s6.heading: Sharing and retention
s6.body:
We share data only with parties that need it to operate the service:

- Web3Forms, to deliver the contact message to our email
- Vercel, to host the site
- Google (Analytics and AdSense) and Microsoft (Clarity), for audience and ads
- Clerk, only if you use sign-in when it is available

Contact messages are kept as long as needed to reply and to meet legal duties, then deleted or no longer tied to you. We do not keep a server database of generated CPF numbers, because that generation does not pass through the server.

s7.heading: Your rights
s7.body:
Where Brazil’s Law 13.709/2018 applies, you may request confirmation, access, correction, anonymization, portability, deletion of unnecessary data, and information about sharing.

Send the request to [contact@example.com](mailto:contact@example.com) with the subject “Privacy” and the email you used on the form, if any. We may ask for the minimum needed to confirm the request is yours. You may also contact Brazil’s national data protection authority.

Visitors elsewhere may have additional rights under their own law.

s8.heading: What we do not do
s8.body:
We do not buy or sell databases of CPF, CNPJ, or other documents. We do not query the Brazilian tax authority from the tools. We do not ask you to upload a real document to “unlock” a generator.

A number produced here is test data. Treat it as a fixture, not as an identity.

The site is not directed at children. We do not knowingly collect a child’s data. If you believe a contact message includes a minor’s data, ask for deletion at the email above.

s1.body:
devKit provides online tools and supporting text for development, testing, staging, and study. Basic use is free and the service is provided as it is. We may change, remove, or interrupt a tool, an article, or the whole site without individual notice.

There is no guarantee of continuous availability, of compatibility with your system, or that a result is fit for a use these terms forbid.

s2.heading: Allowed use
s2.body:
You may use the generators and validators for legitimate software engineering and learning:

- fill staging forms and automated tests
- build fixtures, seeds, and samples in technical docs
- study a format, a mask, and a check digit
- inspect a JWT, JSON, Base64, a QR code, or an HTTP status in your own environment

The result must stay in a test, study, or technical-draft context. Do not present the value as a document of a real person or company.

s3.heading: Nature of generated data
s3.body:
CPF, CNPJ, RG, driver’s-license samples, IBAN, SSN, VAT, names, and addresses produced here are synthetic. A check digit can match without the number existing at the tax authority, a bank, or any official registry.

Mathematical validity is not permission to use the value. It is not a certificate and it does not prove that a person or company exists.

s4.heading: Prohibited use
s4.body:
You must not use the site, the content, or any result for:

- fraud, scams, or false documents
- opening or changing an account, benefit, real invoice, real bill, or contract in someone else’s name
- submitting an invalid document to a bank, carrier, marketplace, or public agency
- spam, phishing, social engineering, or intrusion
- automated load that harms other visitors

We may block access and cooperate with authorities when there is a sign of illegal use. The ban applies even if the tool “accepts” the number.

s5.heading: Intellectual property
s5.body:
The devKit name, layout, original text, and site code are protected. You may use the tools under these terms and quote a page with a link to the source.

Do not bulk-copy the site and republish it as your own, and do not resell access. Sample code published on a tool page may be used in your test project; that does not transfer the brand.

s6.heading: Limitation of liability
s6.body:
To the extent Brazilian law allows, devKit is not liable for damage from misuse, from a decision based on a synthetic number, from service interruption, or from third-party content (ads, analytics, the form processor).

The tools are not legal, accounting, or security advice. Check in your own system whether the format matches the test you need.

The contact form is delivered through Web3Forms. Analytics and session maps use Google and Microsoft, as described in the [Privacy Policy](/privacidade). Those providers are not devKit.

guide.lead: devKit brings together generators, validators, and utilities that run in your browser for software testing, staging, and study. Below is what the site is, who it is for, what it is not, and how to use a result without turning it into a document.
guide.what1: devKit is a free toolkit for people who fill forms, build fixtures, and inspect formats all day. Instead of reusing a real customer’s data in a test environment, you generate a synthetic value with the right mask and, on the same page, read what that value means.
guide.what2: The catalog covers Brazilian test documents (CPF, CNPJ, RG, and a person generator), codes (QR, barcodes, digitable lines, OCR), international references (IBAN, SSN, VAT), and developer utilities (JWT, Base64, JSON, cURL, HTTP status). There is also a Pomodoro timer and simple calculators. Each item opens a page with the control and an explanation, not only a link.
guide.what3: No account is required. The [About](/sobre) page says who runs the site; [Contact](/contato) is the channel for bugs and privacy; [Privacy](/privacidade) and [Terms](/termos) describe data and allowed use.

qa.body: Build scenarios without production PII: a numeric CNPJ, a sample boleto, an IBAN with a checksum, a QR code for a staging URL. The goal is for the app to react to the format, not to simulate an identity.

student.title: Students
student.body: The pages explain the math next to the button. You can study masks, check digits, the difference between Base64 and secrecy, and the HTTP status table with what each range means.

guide.not1: devKit is not Brazil’s tax authority, does not query an official registry, and does not issue documents. A generated CPF or CNPJ can have correct check digits and still not exist as a person or company record. Mathematical validity is not permission to use the number in the real world.
guide.not2: Do not use the results for fraud, account opening, invoices, contracts, or impersonation. That is forbidden by the [Terms of Use](/termos) and may be a crime. Test data stays in a test environment. If you need a real document, stop and use the competent agency.
guide.howDescription: Pick a tool, generate or validate in the browser, and use the result only for testing or study.
guide.howIntro: The flow is the same across most of the catalog. Four steps avoid the most common and most dangerous mistake: treating a test number as a document.
guide.step1Text: Use search, shortcuts, or the categories on this page. The card summarizes the job; the tool page explains format, options, and limits.
guide.step2Name: Generate or validate in the browser
guide.step2Text: Set the mask, quantity, or QR text and press the button. The calculation happens on your device. Copy the result next.
guide.step3Name: Use it only for testing and study
guide.step3Text: Paste it into a fixture, a staging form, or an exercise. Do not publish the value as if it were a real person’s document.
guide.step4Text: CPF and CNPJ have a validator on the tool or on a neighboring page. The blog and each page’s text describe the algorithm when it changes how you should test.
guide.highlightsIntro: Six pages cover most of the use. Each one has its own text about the format and what the result does not prove.
guide.h1Body: Builds numbers with both modulo-11 check digits, with or without a mask. Use it to test inputs, form validation, and sign-up seeds. The page is clear that “valid” here means the math checks out, not that the number is registered, and it links to the validator for a number you already have.
guide.h2Body: Produces a numeric CNPJ with the right digits, with or without the 00.000.000/0001-00 punctuation. Product teams use it for company sign-up, sample boletos, and B2B checkout. The result is synthetic: the tool does not query the tax registry and does not prove a company exists.
guide.h3Body: Turns a URL, text, Wi-Fi network, email, or phone number into an image you can download immediately, with adjustable size and error correction. Dynamic QR, on the neighboring page, stores destination, status, and expiry in your browser so you can change the link without reprinting the artwork.
guide.h4Body: Encodes and decodes text and files in the browser, with a preview when the content is an image. Use it to inspect a data URI or a payload without uploading the file. The page treats Base64 as encoding: anyone who sees the string can reverse it, so it is not secrecy.
guide.h5Body: Splits header, payload, and signature so you can read the claims. With an HS256 secret you can check the signature locally and mint a sample token. The token you paste is not sent to devKit; the tool does not replace your production identity provider.
guide.h6Body: In one click, builds a fictional pack for a long form: name, CPF, RG, driver’s license, address, and sample contacts. It is the shortcut when a staging sign-up needs every field. No field points at a real person; the tool page describes each block.
guide.trustTitle: Generated in the browser, without uploading your test
guide.trust1: CPF, CNPJ, QR text, JWT, and Base64 files are processed in your browser. devKit does not receive that content just because you clicked generate. History and favorites, when they exist, stay in local storage and leave when you clear site data.
guide.trust2: What can leave the device is the visit itself: pages viewed, audience measurement, ads, and, if you fill it in, the contact form. Details are in the [Privacy Policy](/privacidade). The public email is [contact@example.com](mailto:contact@example.com), also listed on [Contact](/contato).
guide.faq1q: Is a generated CPF a real person?
guide.faq1a: No. It follows modulo 11 and may pass a form check, but it is not looked up at the tax authority and it does not represent a registry record. Use it only for testing and study.
guide.faq2q: Does devKit upload what I generate?
guide.faq2a: Not because you used the tool. The calculation stays in the browser. The contact form, analytics, and ads are a separate flow, described in the privacy policy.
guide.faq3q: Can I use the number to open an account or issue an invoice?
guide.faq3a: No. That use is forbidden and may be fraud. The terms limit the result to testing, staging, and learning.
guide.faq4a: Not to use the tools. Search, generation, and validation work without sign-up. Favorites are stored in this browser.

A custom domain is for when the app requires a specific host, such as the company domain in staging. Confirm that you control that DNS. Addresses at public providers may belong to real people — do not use this tool to generate them in bulk.
seo.formatsIntro: The part before the @ changes with the format. Every address is lowercase and without accents, so it pastes into CSV, JSON and databases without encoding issues.
seo.formatNomeSobrenome: First and last name produces something like joao.silva@example.com.
seo.formatUnderline: First_last swaps the dot for an underscore: joao_silva@example.com.
seo.formatInicial: Initial and last name shortens the first name: j.silva@example.com.
seo.formatNumero: Name and number adds four digits: ana.4821@example.com.
seo.formatAleatorio: Random builds a string with no name, useful when the test must not look like a person.
seo.how2: Choose the local-part format: first and last name, underscore, initial, name with a number, or a random string.
seo.how3: Keep a test domain or enter a custom domain you control.
seo.how4Before: Click Generate emails and copy one address or the whole list. For a record with a name and documents, use the
seo.localBody: The draw of the name, the number and the chosen domain happens in your browser. devKit does not receive the list, does not store the addresses on a server and does not send email. History for this tool, after you generate again, stays in this browser’s local storage and disappears when you clear the site data.
seo.practice1: Use it only in development, QA, staging and study.
seo.practice2: Do not register the address as a real customer contact, invoice, account or production password recovery.
seo.practice3: Prefer reserved domains when the test does not need to receive email.
seo.practice4: Delete fixtures and the local history at the end of the test cycle.

faq.q1: Does the generated email receive messages?
faq.a1: No. The address is fake. example.com, example.org and example.net are reserved and do not point to inboxes. devKit does not create an account, forward email or show received messages.
faq.q2: Can I use it in production?
faq.a2: Not as a person’s contact. Use generation in development, staging and automated tests. In production, ask for an email the user controls.
faq.a3: For most tests, example.com. If the system rejects that domain, use example.org, example.net or a name ending in .test. Use a custom domain only when you control the DNS or accept the risk that the address exists.
faq.q4: Does the data leave my browser?
faq.a4: Not by using the tool. The list is built in the browser. History stays in this device’s local storage.
faq.q5: Why are there no accents in the names?
faq.a5: The local part uses only unaccented letters, numbers and the dot and underscore separators. The address then pastes into forms, CSV and databases without encoding problems.
faq.a6: No. Temporary email is a mailbox that receives messages for a few minutes. Here you only get a synthetic address to fill a field. Nothing is delivered and nothing can be read.

seo.algoP1: A CPF has 11 digits: 9 base + 2 check digits. Each check digit is obtained by multiplying previous digits by weights, summing, applying mod 11, and treating remainder 10 or 11 as 0. Sequences with all identical digits (e.g. 111.111.111-11) are rejected even if mod 11 “closes”.
seo.algoP2: The ninth base digit historically indicates the tax region of issue (e.g. 8 for SP). Useful for regional demos, but it does not prove the document’s real origin.
seo.whatBody: Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas is Brazil’s individual tax identifier. In software, mathematical validation avoids junk in forms; checking official existence is a separate step, done via authorized integrations when needed.
seo.practice1: Use only in test and development environments.
seo.practice2: Do not use generated numbers to open accounts or commit fraud.
seo.practice3: Prefer local generation when you do not need to persist data.

faq.q6: What is the difference between masked and unmasked CPF?
faq.a6: Masked format is 000.000.000-00 (human-readable). Unmasked is just the 11 digits, better for APIs, databases, and fixtures.
